$comment: Expiring SAST waivers (none shipped). Prefer a permanent, code-owned inline suppression on the flagged line: `// nosemgrep: <rule-id> -- <reason>`, always naming the exact rule id (never a bare nosemgrep). Use this register only for a temporary waiver that must lapse: each entry names the rule, the path AND the flagged code: fingerprint = sha256 of the flagged source lines, each stripped, joined by newlines (`python3 tools/ci/scripts/sast-gate.py --fingerprint <path> <line> [<end>]`). The waiver covers that code only: a new finding of the same rule elsewhere in the file blocks, and changing the flagged code makes it block again; moving it (edits above it) does not. `line` (exact start line) is enforced only for an entry without a fingerprint; `lineAtApproval` and `code` are for reviewers. Whole-file entries are not honoured and fail supply-chain:lint. Fields: rule, path, fingerprint or line, reason and expires (both required, expires at most 90 days ahead; supply-chain:lint), approvedBy (a role, for reviewers). After `expires` the waiver is no longer applied and the finding blocks again. With gate integrity enabled, changing this file is a gate-defining change (Maintainer approval, ADR 0410).
